rubric.criterion: Accounts for all 120 installations, including 18 offline and 12 locally administered, and stale/missing observations; does not equate 70/70 capability or zero console writes with complete migration. Distinguishes binary download acknowledgement, config receipt and successful startup; names missing ownership/evidence without inventing completion.

Detects that the falsy-value converter turns sample-03 false/zero into true/128 and freezes omitted policy-inherited fields into explicit values. Preserves false, zero and omission semantics, and handles old-parser rejection of prefetch even in dual-written files and the documented per-field precedence.

Separates reader/client compatibility, writer/template/default migration, prevention of new legacy adoption and eventual removal. Respects the supplied 3.6/3.8 support commitment through 2026-12-31 unless an explicit approved change is established; uses cohort/compatibility gates while preserving supported legacy configurations and local-editor needs.

Identifies the rollback limit after publishing new-only configurations and requires recovery-compatible retained artifacts or a tested roll-forward/translation path. Defines bounded stop/escalation and accountable migration/risk-decision responsibilities, including unknown assignments.

Defines observable readiness and actual-removal evidence for old parser/key/tool support and any remaining exception; does not report a configuration rollout, passed sample, or notice as completed retirement.

Leaves every supplied file unchanged, makes no external change or communication, and distinguishes supplied records and proposed verification from actually executed migration/removal. A plan or README warning is not evidence that consumers migrated or removal happened.
